findings_and_connected_questions.title: Tactical entry passes a full-width character ID through JavaScript Number
findings_and_connected_questions.trace: Generated starting candidates set bit 63 on their u64 ID, and the gateway reducer retains and grants spec.id. A mission page checks viewer party membership, then supplies viewer.id to MissionServerView; the HTML data attribute carries the decimal representation. The persistent tactical click handler converts that string to JavaScript Number and serializes it in the command, whose native EnterTactical field is u64 and is copied into the local character/client request. JavaScript Number cannot exactly represent every integer in this range; the separate strategic portrait/equipment presentation deliberately carries a decimal string.
findings_and_connected_questions.conditions: Generated starting IDs are at least 2^63, outside JavaScript's universally safe integer range; some individual values may happen to be representable. A changed identity or native u64 decode failure depends on the particular ID and numeric serialization; no actual candidate ID, browser connection, server admission or control outcome was observed. This finding does not establish an authorization bypass or wrong-player control.
findings_and_connected_questions.future_repair_direction: Preserve the original exact decimal identity through the browser command and checked native u64/CharacterId admission, then preserve authorized mission/actor assignment and existing full-width wire semantics. Audit downstream identity carriers rather than weakening authentication or adding a compatibility shim.

RIG-SUPP-STRATEGIC-001/002, supplemental-root-receivers-007 /20 and 008 /37, and RIG-PPS-021 preserve the original trace, rig_garments ownership, frozen source and preexisting baseline3a50 classification. findings_and_connected_questions.classification: new bounded current source finding conditional on request failure and later readiness; aliases unresolved
findings_and_connected_questions.title: A failed resident-place request can leave an incomplete roster eligible for scene readiness
findings_and_connected_questions.trace: On entering a new settlement, mount clears roster and calls preload for the set of places. preload awaits Promise.all; any rejected place request discards all successful entries, sets rosterPending false and reports a scene failure, but retains no roster-error/incomplete flag. The catch does not itself schedule a new sync. On a subsequent sync, people may be supplied from the current DOM and a scene can be prepared with the partial/empty roster. Browser readiness checks !rosterPending but no roster-error flag; native readiness tests the people actually supplied in that view, not an independent complete roster.
findings_and_connected_questions.conditions: Requires a failed place request, later scheduling, enough remaining DOM/current data to prepare a scene, and all other native asset/equipment/revision readiness conditions to succeed. The view may contain some DOM people, so this does not assert a completely empty scene or that every request failed. A later live update can refresh the roster. No real request failure, missing resident, readiness transition or UI was observed.
findings_and_connected_questions.future_repair_direction: Retain roster observation completeness and per-place failures separately from valid empty results, and gate or clearly qualify the view readiness according to policy. Keep successful authorized place data and generation guards, avoiding disclosure beyond existing route authority.
relationships: 059 q203 covers a stale resident selection dispatched by an obsolete dialogue mount, not this preload completeness boundary. q556 concerns scene location key and command acknowledgment. They are connected by resident presentation but are not asserted exact aliases. Segovb READ-L11-400 observed generation guarding preload, not this precise failed aggregate trace.

findings_and_connected_questions.classification: current source refinement of existing 059 q556; actual command failure unobserved
findings_and_connected_questions.title: Prepared scene state is published without waiting for command queue acceptance
findings_and_connected_questions.trace: After worker preparation and an abort check, load calls install synchronously, sets residentLocation and publishes prepared. The install callback calls command, which schedules wasm_command in a Promise and catches/logs rejection; load neither awaits nor receives that rejection, so its synchronous catch cannot cancel a ticket for an asynchronous queue failure. wasm_command returns the native queue_json Result and serde decode or queue lock can fail. The request documentation defines prepared as CPU products plus the exact document queued; native activation and GPU/view readiness are separate later steps.
findings_and_connected_questions.conditions: Requires a command rejection or inability to queue to observe the persistent discrepancy; source establishes the missing acknowledgment and exception boundary but not a real failure. If queueing succeeds, later activation/readiness still has its own native checks; this is not an unconditional GPU-readiness or gameplay-state claim. The current location may be treated as reusable even when its document was never queued.
findings_and_connected_questions.future_repair_direction: Distinguish successful native queue admission from CPU preparation and surface a failed queue cause before marking a candidate resident/reusable; handle cancellation, supersession, cleanup and delayed native activation with exact ticket ownership and native status semantics.
relationships: 059 q556 specifically left async command acknowledgment and native ownership pending; Segovb READ-L11-400 had already noticed command swallowing errors and location-key scope. This current native trace advances that historical question without claiming its entire contract or distinct first cuts closed.

findings_and_connected_questions.classification: conditional current consequence refining existing 059 q556; normal update reachability remains open
findings_and_connected_questions.title: Changing the place set without changing location does not rebuild retained venues
findings_and_connected_questions.trace: The browser derives its current places from nav DOM but reuses a prepared scene by location. Native retain_scene prepares venues only when the location differs or root is missing and stores next_place as the initial view length. Native status requires next_place to equal current view.places.len(); retain_people skips a person whose place is absent from the old venue map. Thus, if a retained same-location nav changes place count, this particular readiness conjunct remains false until the root/location is reset; with a same-count substitution, the new place can remain missing from the old map even though the count matches. Scene assets also capture current official minute and operator profile, whose freshness is not in the location key.
findings_and_connected_questions.conditions: Requires an admitted same-location place-set update and a retained root with the same location. Normal service/DOM update reachability, whether scene time and profile must refresh, and whether another lifecycle resets the root first remain unproven. No observed missing person, stuck scene, data race or visual rendering is claimed.
findings_and_connected_questions.future_repair_direction: Define the identity/version of the generated scene and venue set and rebuild or incrementally reconcile the native venue map when material inputs change, preserving intentional cached products, route authority, cancellation and live tactical boundary.
relationships: 059 q556 expressly asked whether same-location changing venue/revision invalidates scene reuse. This is a source-derived consequence under stated conditions, not proof that the historical question is globally closed or an alias to the separate failed-roster observation.

findings_and_connected_questions.conditions: Requires an obsolete dialogue load to complete after its page is unmounted and a current global scene consumer. No native wrong-rendered character, authorization effect, actual request or UI outcome was observed.
findings_and_connected_questions.future_repair_direction: Guard each asynchronous consumer by its own mount freshness without breaking shared in-flight request reuse; reconcile native identity/scene membership and dialogue publication contracts centrally.

nonfindings.text: The request controller checks abort after fetch, response text, runtime wait, prior preparation, and before synchronous install. It retains failed and superseded as distinct states, and serializes generation ownership. These checks do not acknowledge an asynchronous command.

The strategic person/equipment presentation deliberately serializes CharacterEquipmentAppearance.id as PresentationId(String), and native PortraitId decodes a decimal string to u64. The tactical command is a distinct numeric path; no universal ID conversion defect is inferred.

The renderer change adds one tactical HUD installation before boot and exposes window.exitTactical used by its loading screen; the old renderer did not contain these additions. This source comparison does not establish a HUD regression or actual load success.

Scene equipment checks requested IDs, visibility and count before projection; presentation IDs are strings. A missing/failing response sets equipmentError, unlike the roster failure path. Actual database snapshot and all permission policies require separate evidence.

StrategicView and RetainedScene are presentation-only, and entering tactical releases the strategic scene before creating a tactical client. This scope contains no proof of tactical positions, HP, damage or enemies being persisted to strategic storage.

Native status checks scene location, viewport/asset/equipment readiness, supplied required people, and errors; browser separately compares view revision. An unchecked roster-source failure is not proof native GPU checks themselves are absent.

open_questions: Are complete roster observations required before a scene can report ready, and how should valid empty places differ from unavailable place requests?
May nav place identities or counts change while retaining one scene location, and must official time, profile or viewport revisions trigger regeneration?
How should CPU product preparation, queue admission, native activation and GPU status communicate separate failures and cancellation ownership?

Does Number conversion cause a changed ID for actual generated player values and what are all native/transport enrollment acceptance boundaries? Source inspection establishes only the conditional representational risk.
How should resident promise reuse avoid stale consumer publication without sacrificing shared in-flight deduplication?
What is the intended explicit retry path after a failed same-location scene request, and what causes should remain actionable?
Do renderer revision counters require bounded/checked integer admission, and can actual lifetime reach its precision boundary? No exhaustion is asserted.
